findings.quote: If `DATABASE_URL` is already set and `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'select 1'` succeeds, print it and exit 0 (CI with a `postgres:16` service container passes `PG_SUPER_URL` and the script only needs to run the shim + `createdb`).
findings.problem: The ordered behaviour list (3.1–3.7) has no CI path: item 3.2 exits early on `DATABASE_URL`, but CI sets `PG_SUPER_URL`, not `DATABASE_URL`, so as written CI falls through to Path A/B (`pg_ctlcluster`/`initdb` on the runner) and fails. The `PG_SUPER_URL` contract appears only in Build 9, and `createdb -O churchapp_owner churchapp` (3.5) is a bare CLI call that has no connection parameters for a URL-based superuser. Two agents will wire this differently and one of them will break the CI job that 1.1 already fixed to this variable name.
findings.fix: Insert a new item after 3.2: '3.2b Path 0 (CI / any reachable superuser): when `PG_SUPER_URL` is set, use it for every superuser statement (`psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 …`), skip Paths A and B, and derive `DATABASE_URL` by replacing the user/password/database in `PG_SUPER_URL` with `churchapp_owner:churchapp` / `churchapp`.' Rewrite 3.5 to use one helper for all paths: `super_sql() { case "$MODE" in url) psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; cluster) sudo -u postgres psql -p "$PORT" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; initdb) psql "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PORT/postgres" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; esac; }` and replace `createdb -O churchapp_owner churchapp` with `super_sql -tAc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = 'churchapp'" | grep -q 1 || super_sql -c "create database churchapp owner churchapp_owner"`. Build 9 then only says 'the CI job sets `PG_SUPER_URL` (Path 0)'.

findings.quote: create the role first with a tiny inline `do $$ … create role churchapp_owner … $$`, then `createdb -O churchapp_owner churchapp` if it does not exist, then apply the full shim
findings.problem: The shim guards every role with `if not exists`, so if the inline pre-creation makes `churchapp_owner` with fewer attributes than the shim specifies (the natural reading of 'tiny'), the shim skips it and the role never gets `bypassrls` or the dev password; Verify's `t|f` check and Path A's TCP login then fail. The prompt also still contains the drafter's thinking aloud ('apply … ONLY for the role statements? No — keep it simple').
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Create the role before the database, with its full attributes, in one guarded statement: `do $$ begin if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = ''churchapp_owner'') then create role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password ''churchapp''; end if; end $$;` — and make the shim''s own `churchapp_owner` block follow the guard with `alter role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password ''churchapp''` unconditionally, so attributes converge even when the role pre-exists. Then create the database if missing, then apply the full shim against `churchapp`.' Delete the 'ONLY for the role statements? No —' sentence.

findings.quote: Path B (if A fails — no cluster, no permission): as the `postgres` OS user when root, else the current user: `initdb -D "$STATE_DIR/pg" -A trust -U postgres --no-locale -E UTF8`
findings.problem: When the agent is root, `initdb` and `pg_ctl` must run as the `postgres` OS user, but `$STATE_DIR` is `<repo>/.local-pg` inside a directory the `postgres` user usually cannot traverse or write (`/root/…` or a 700 home). The same applies to Path A: `sudo -u postgres psql -f supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` needs the `postgres` user to read a file inside the repo. PLAN 'Environment facts' says cluster `main` is down, so the fallback is the likely path on the founder's agents, and it fails as written.
findings.fix: Add to 3.4: 'Before `initdb`, `mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"`; if running as root, `chown postgres "$STATE_DIR"` and, when `sudo -u postgres test -w "$STATE_DIR"` still fails (untraversable parents), use `PGDATA_DIR="${LOCAL_PG_DATA:-/var/lib/postgresql/churchapp-local}"` instead and record the path in `$STATE_DIR/PGDATA` — the URL files stay in `.local-pg/`.' Add to 3.3/3.5: 'Never pass repo file paths to `sudo -u postgres psql -f`; feed SQL on stdin (`sudo -u postgres psql … -f - < "$REPO_ROOT/supabase/tests/00_shim.sql"`).' Mention both in docs/ENV.md's Local database section.

findings.quote: (g) any function definition (search from `create or replace function` to the next `$$`-terminated body or `;`) lacks both `security definer` and `set search_path = ''`
findings.problem: 'Lacks both' fires only when neither clause is present, so a function with `security definer` but no `set search_path = ''` (or vice versa) passes the checker. DESIGN §12 and PLAN §12 require every function to have both, and 1.4a's `08_rerunnable.sql` and the security checklist assume the checker enforces it.
findings.fix: Rewrite (g): 'any function definition (from `create or replace function` to the end of its body) that lacks `security definer` OR lacks `set search_path = ''` — report which clause is missing.' Extend `--self-test` to include one snippet missing only `security definer` and one missing only `set search_path`.

findings.quote: Verify with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'select current_user, current_setting("server_version")'` (use single quotes correctly in bash).
findings.problem: Double quotes inside SQL are identifier quotes, so `current_setting("server_version")` errors with 'column "server_version" does not exist'; the parenthetical admits the quoting is wrong but leaves the wrong text for the agent to copy.
findings.fix: Write: `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select current_user || ' ' || current_setting('server_version')"` → `churchapp_owner 16.x`.

findings.quote: otherwise executes `select org_id from public.<parent> where id = $1` via `execute format(…, tg_argv[1]) using <fk value>`
findings.problem: The FK column name arrives as text in `tg_argv[0]`, and plpgsql cannot write `new.<variable>`; the prompt does not say how to read the dynamic column, so agents pick between `to_jsonb(new) ->> tg_argv[0]`, `hstore`, or a per-table function — the hstore variant needs an extension that is not created.
findings.fix: Append: 'Read the FK value with `(to_jsonb(new) ->> tg_argv[0])::uuid` (no extension needed); the parent lookup is `execute format(''select org_id from public.%I where id = $1'', tg_argv[1]) into parent_org using fk_value`.'

findings.quote: Add a `--self-test` flag that runs the checker against a few inline bad snippets written to a temp dir under the scratchpad
findings.problem: 'The scratchpad' is a per-session directory the script cannot know about; a committed script must not depend on it, and the Constraints forbid `/tmp`.
findings.fix: Write: 'written to `$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg/rerun-selftest/` (created and emptied by the script; gitignored)'.

findings.quote: - `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select rolbypassrls, rolsuper from pg_roles where rolname = current_user"` → `t|f`.
findings.problem: Every Verify command uses `$DATABASE_URL`, but the prompt never tells the agent to export it (local-up.sh only prints the `export …` line); a fresh agent runs the checks with an empty variable and gets connection errors.
findings.fix: Add as the first Verify bullet: '`export DATABASE_URL="$(cat .local-pg/DATABASE_URL)"` (or `eval "$(bash scripts/db/local-up.sh | tail -n 1)"`) before the psql checks.'

findings.quote: Write it to `$STATE_DIR/DATABASE_URL` and to `$STATE_DIR/PG_SUPER_URL`
findings.problem: In Path A (Debian cluster, peer auth) there is no superuser URL the current user can use — superuser access is `sudo -u postgres psql` — so `$STATE_DIR/PG_SUPER_URL` would hold a URL that only works as the `postgres` OS user. G3's 1.4a already plans `psql "$(cat .local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL)" -c "drop database churchapp"`.
findings.fix: Write: 'Write `$STATE_DIR/DATABASE_URL` always; write `$STATE_DIR/PG_SUPER_URL` only in Path 0 and Path B (where a URL works); in Path A write `$STATE_DIR/SUPER_PSQL=sudo -u postgres psql -p <port>` instead, and expose `super_psql` in `scripts/db/_env.sh` so later scripts (1.4a''s reset, 1.5''s seed) call `super_psql -c …` regardless of path.'

findings.quote: `documents` (`id, org_id, title, description, category text, audience_group_id fk set null, storage_path` (check `…/documents/…`, unique)`, mime_type, file_size_bytes, publish_at default now(), created_by, created_at, updated_at`)
findings.problem: Unbalanced backticks split the column list; the path check is elided with `…`, unlike bulletins where it is spelled out, so agents may write a different pattern.
findings.fix: Replace with: '`documents` (`id, org_id, title, description, category text, audience_group_id fk set null, storage_path text not null, mime_type, file_size_bytes, publish_at default now(), created_by, created_at, updated_at`; check `storage_path like org_id::text || ''/documents/'' || id::text || ''/%''`; unique index on `storage_path`)'.

findings.quote: if the caller is not a directory admin of `new.org_id` and not super admin, forbid changing `congregation_status`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, `household_role` to anything other than `child`/`other`, and `user_id` to anything except `auth.uid()` or null
findings.problem: Two flows the same group specifies cannot pass this guard: `accept_invitation` (1.3b item 6) runs as a non-admin caller and inserts a person with `household_role = 'head'` and `user_id = auth.uid()`; `srv_attach_user` (1.3b item 13) runs as `service_role` with `auth.uid()` null (so `is_directory_admin` is false) and inserts `head` + a foreign `user_id`. The 1.3b smoke test 2 therefore fails with `household_role_not_allowed`/`field_not_editable`. 'Changing' is also undefined for `before insert` (no `old`). G3's helpers.sql explicitly asks whether the guards trust a null `auth.uid()`; the prompt never answers.
findings.fix: Rewrite the item: 'Skip the guard entirely when `auth.uid() is null` (owner, service role, cron, seed — RLS and grants already keep anon out) or when `current_setting(''app.trusted_rpc'', true) = ''on''` (set with `perform set_config(''app.trusted_rpc'', ''on'', true)` at the top of `accept_invitation` and `srv_attach_user`, which build persons under their own rules). Otherwise, for non-admins: on INSERT compare against the column defaults (`attendee`, null, null, `other`, null); on UPDATE compare `new` with `old`; forbid … (as written).' State the same two skips for `guard_household_privacy_columns` (the household insert in `accept_invitation`/`srv_attach_user` must still get `hide_from_fellowship = true` when `created_via = ''admin''`). Add `app.trusted_rpc` to the section (5) convention comment and to open_issues so 1.4b/1.4c test both the guard and the bypass.

findings.quote: write these two functions in `plpgsql` and place them AFTER section (6) inside a clearly labelled "(6b) storage helpers — must follow the views" sub-section, or make them reference the base tables plus `app.household_view_level` directly; either is acceptable, say which in a comment
findings.problem: The two options are not behaviourally equivalent: the views also apply `directory_listed`, `deceased_on`, `congregation_status <> 'inactive'` and the fellowship adults-only rule, so a photo of an unlisted person or a child is readable under one implementation and not the other. Two agents produce incompatible security behaviour and 1.4c's `07_storage_billing_audit.sql` cannot know which to assert.
findings.fix: Pick one: 'Write `can_read_object`/`can_write_object` in plpgsql in sub-section (6b) immediately after the views, and for `directory-photos` decide readability by `exists (select 1 from public.directory_households where id = <hh>)` / `exists (select 1 from public.directory_persons where id = <person>)` so photo visibility always equals directory visibility.' Delete the alternative.

findings.quote: as `churchapp_owner`, using `set local role authenticated` + `select set_config('request.jwt.claims', …, true)` to impersonate — the pattern 1.4 will put in `helpers.sql`
findings.problem: At 1.3a no table grants exist for `authenticated` (section 9 is 1.4a and section (1) revoked default privileges), so every smoke step that inserts or updates as the impersonated user (`update households …`, `insert … events`, `delete from org_membership_permissions`) fails with 42501 permission denied on the table, not with the trigger error the step expects. The same smoke-script instruction appears in 1.3b.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Stay connected as `churchapp_owner` (bypassrls; no policies exist yet) and impersonate only by setting the claims: `select set_config(''request.jwt.claims'', json_build_object(''sub'', <uid>, ''role'', ''authenticated'')::text, true)`; `auth.uid()` and every `app.*` helper read those claims, so trigger and view behaviour is what is under test. Do not `set local role authenticated` until 1.4a has issued the grants. Clear the claims with `set_config(''request.jwt.claims'', '''', true)` between users.' Apply the same wording to 1.3b's smoke preamble (its RPCs are security definer, so calling them as the owner without `grant execute` is fine).

findings.quote: `app.rate_limit_hit(key text, max_hits int, window_len interval) returns boolean` (plpgsql, volatile): upsert into `private.rate_limits (key, window_start, count)` … increment, and return `count > max_hits`. Step 1.3b uses it in `srv_resolve_share_link`.
findings.problem: 1.3b item 9 needs a read-only check ('check-without-increment before … e.g. a second helper `app.rate_limit_check(key, max)` if needed') so that successful or password-less page loads do not consume the failure budget; leaving it 'if needed' means one agent adds a helper 1.4a's grant list does not know about and another counts every load, locking legitimate viewers out after 10 opens in 15 minutes.
findings.fix: Add to Build 2: '`app.rate_limit_check(key text, max_hits int, window_len interval) returns boolean` (plpgsql, stable): same bucket computation, reads the current bucket without writing and returns `count >= max_hits`.' Change `rate_limit_hit` to return `count >= max_hits` after incrementing (so the 10th failure locks and the 11th attempt is refused, matching 1.3b Verify 4). Include both signatures in the Goal helper list, the function count, HANDOFF and open_issues; 1.3b item 9 then calls `rate_limit_check` first and `rate_limit_hit` only after a wrong password.

findings.quote: write `audit_log (org_id, actor_user_id = auth.uid(), table_name, row_id, action = tg_op, old_data, new_data)`; take `org_id` from the row (`org_id` column, or `id` for `organizations`, null for `super_admins`)
findings.problem: `row_id uuid` has no defined value for tables without a uuid `id`: `organization_settings` (PK `org_id`), `org_membership_permissions` (composite PK), `super_admins` (PK `user_id`). Column subsets for `households`/`persons` are described in prose only, so each agent hard-codes a different mechanism.
findings.fix: Append: '`row_id` = `id` when the table has one, else `org_id` (`organization_settings`), `membership_id` (`org_membership_permissions`), `user_id` (`super_admins`). Pass the audited column list as the trigger argument (`execute function app.audit_row(''hide_from_fellowship,hide_from_congregation,show_children_in_fellowship,privacy_confirmed_at'')`); when `tg_argv[0]` is null store `to_jsonb(old/new)`, otherwise only those keys.'

findings.quote: rate limit FIRST with `app.rate_limit_hit('share:t:' || encode(token_hash, 'hex'), 10, interval '15 minutes')` and `app.rate_limit_hit('share:ip:' || ip_hash, 10, interval '15 minutes')` → `{status: 'rate_limited'}` when either is hit (count only failed attempts: call the counter after a wrong password, and check-without-increment before — implement `app.rate_limit_hit` usage so that reads do not consume the budget, e.g. a second helper `app.rate_limit_check(key, max)` if needed, documented)
findings.problem: The first half says to call the incrementing `rate_limit_hit` at the top of every resolve; the parenthesis says the opposite. Agents following the first half count successful unlocks and password-less loads, so a shared link stops working after 10 views in 15 minutes; the 'if needed' helper is left to chance and to 1.4a's grants.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Check the limits FIRST without counting: `app.rate_limit_check(''share:t:'' || encode(token_hash, ''hex''), 10, interval ''15 minutes'')` and `app.rate_limit_check(''share:ip:'' || ip_hash, 10, interval ''15 minutes'')` (helper from 1.3a) → `{status: ''rate_limited''}` when either is true. Count a failure ONLY on a wrong password: call `app.rate_limit_hit(...)` for both keys before returning `wrong_password`. Successful unlocks, `needs_password` and every other status never touch the counters.'

findings.quote: purge organizations in `cancelled` for more than 30 days by enqueueing `storage_deletions (bucket, object_name = org_id || '/', is_prefix = true)` for each of the five buckets and then deleting the org row
findings.problem: No column records when an organization became `cancelled` (1.2's `organizations` has only `created_at`/`updated_at`, and `updated_at` moves on any edit), so 'more than 30 days' is not computable; agents will guess (`updated_at`, a new column, or skip the purge). 9999 is still unfrozen, so the column belongs in 1.2.
findings.fix: In 1.2 Build 7 (3) add to `organizations`: `cancelled_at timestamptz` (comment: 'set when status becomes cancelled; drives the 30-day purge'). In 1.3a add a tiny `before update of status on organizations` branch (in `app.mirror_subscription_status` or a new `app.stamp_org_status()` trigger function `organizations_stamp_status`) that sets `cancelled_at = now()` when `new.status = ''cancelled'' and old.status <> ''cancelled''` and clears it otherwise. In 1.3b write: 'purge organizations where `status = ''cancelled'' and cancelled_at < now() - interval ''30 days''`'. Record the column in open_issues for G3/G5 (2.2's cancel action relies on the trigger, not on setting it by hand).

findings.quote: when `person_id` is null and the caller has no person in the org, create a one-person household (`created_via = 'invitation'`, `name = display_name`) and a person (`congregation_status = 'attendee'`, `household_role = 'head'`, `user_id = auth.uid()`)
findings.problem: Both `accept_invitation` (non-admin caller) and `srv_attach_user` (service role, `auth.uid()` null) insert persons that 1.3a's `guard_persons_columns` forbids for non-admins (`head` role, foreign `user_id`), so smoke tests 2 and the direct-creation flow fail unless the RPCs opt out of the guard. The prompt says the opposite: 'the column guards from 1.3a still apply (RPCs run with the caller's auth.uid())'.
findings.fix: In items 6 and 13 add as the first statement after the permission checks: '`perform set_config(''app.trusted_rpc'', ''on'', true);` — the 1.3a guards skip while this transaction-local flag is on; the RPC itself is responsible for the rules it enforces (minor check, role `head`).' Change the item-7 sentence to: 'the column guards from 1.3a still apply to `save_person`/`save_household` (they do not set the flag)'. Add to the smoke script: `save_person` by a non-admin setting `household_role = ''head''` on another person → `household_role_not_allowed`, proving the guard is still active outside the flagged RPCs.

findings.quote: → `sermon_id uuid, label text, password text, expires_at timestamptz, max_views integer`
findings.problem: `pg_get_function_identity_arguments` prints the SQL-standard type name `timestamp with time zone`, never `timestamptz`; an agent comparing literally reports a mismatch.
findings.fix: Write the expected output as `sermon_id uuid, label text, password text, expires_at timestamp with time zone, max_views integer`.

findings.quote: wrong password ×10 → the 11th returns `rate_limited`
findings.problem: With 1.3a's `count > max_hits` semantics the 10th failure leaves count = 10, the 11th attempt is still evaluated (and only then pushes count to 11), so `rate_limited` first appears on the 12th call; PLAN §12 says '10 wrong passwords lock the token'.
findings.fix: Keep the Verify text and make the helpers match it (1.3a fix: `rate_limit_check` returns `count >= max_hits`, `rate_limit_hit` returns `count >= max_hits` after incrementing); add to Verify 4: 'the 10th wrong attempt returns `wrong_password`, the 11th returns `rate_limited` without evaluating the password'.

findings.quote: `set local app.cascade = 'on'` (so `guard_last_org_manager` audits instead of blocking)
findings.problem: `set local` is a SQL utility command that cannot take effect per iteration inside a plpgsql loop the way the prompt implies, and it is not the form the 1.3a guard reads (`current_setting('app.cascade', true)`); agents may use `set app.cascade` (session-wide, leaks to the pooled connection) instead.
findings.fix: Write: '`perform set_config(''app.cascade'', ''on'', true)` at the start of the function (transaction-local; PostgREST wraps each RPC in its own transaction, so it cannot leak) and the same in the org-purge branch of `srv_housekeeping`.'
